Hi Hannah —

Thanks for the introductory call today. Per our discussion I promised to capture the key asks here so we can align on a MAP and a timeline for a decision between Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployment. High level asks from our side:

- Data residency: all PHI must remain within US regions; would like a clear timeline for Private or VPC options.
- Performance: sub-200ms P99 for short inference (<= 128 tokens) is a soft target.
- Timeline: procurement wants a 10-week path to production if we go Dedicated; need comparative lead-times for Hosted and Private.

Can you share a mutual action plan artifact and a rough decision cadence so we can present to our technical procurement on Thursday? Also include any SOC2 / audit artifacts needed for the security review.

Tom — thanks, this is helpful. Short reply with a suggested path and an attached starter MAP.

Recommendation (quick):
- Phase 1 (0–3 weeks): Proof-of-concept on Hosted (fastest to spin up; no infra lead-time). Demo with your telemetry and a small prompt set.
- Phase 2 (3–7 weeks): Parallel Dedicated sizing evaluation (throughput runs) if committed to predictable QPS. We reserve capacity in the desired region (US-East / US-West).
- Phase 3 (7–10+ weeks): Private/VPC option for full data residency & managed control plane — longer lead time due to network setup and KMS/HSM integration.

Why this order: Hosted proves the UX and output quality quickly; Dedicated buys you SLA and predictability; Private is for strict residency/compliance but requires longer ops coordination.

I attached a draft MAP (Orchard_MAP_v1.xlsx) that maps milestones, owners, and acceptance criteria. I also attached a SOC2 snapshot we can use in your vendor review pack.

Next steps I propose:
- Review the MAP with your procurement on Thursday (you scheduled?)
- Karthik will run a short perf bench on Dedicated once we confirm expected QPS / token distribution.
- We’ll publish a price band and estimated lead-times for Private by Wednesday.

Attachments:
- Orchard_MAP_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)
- SOC2_snapshot.pdf (document)

Thanks — I’ll join the Thursday call if you want.

Best,
Hannah

Adding a few engineering notes for Orchard and Hannah —

1) Bench inputs we need from Orchard ASAP: expected concurrent requests, average prompt length, and top-10 inference endpoints (so we can size KV cache benefits). If you can provide representative traces or a small sample workload that would accelerate Dedicated sizing.

2) Dedicated vs Hosted perf delta: in our experience for short prompts Hosted P99 is often similar to Dedicated at modest QPS, but Dedicated scales better at sustained high QPS. If Orchard expects bursty peaks (e.g., >400 QPS) we should design for Dedicated.

3) Private lead time: estimate 6–8 weeks after signed SOW for a standard VPC + KMS setup in a US region; if an on-prem appliance is required we should estimate 10–12 weeks.

4) Redlines: attached a short SLA_note.pdf and SOW_redlines.pdf—these call out availability commitments and acceptable outage credit bands. Hannah — happy to join procurement meeting to walk tech assumptions.

Attachments:
- SLA_note.pdf
- SOW_redlines.pdf

—Karthik

Hi Jane / Tom —

Appreciate the checklist — attaching an updated MAP that includes procurement checkpoints, retention acceptance criteria, and a price band for all three lanes: Hosted (subscription + usage), Dedicated (monthly reserved capacity + burst), and Private (one-time setup + monthly support). Summary highlights below: 

- Hosted: fastest path — 1–2 weeks to POC, retention configurable (default 30 days, can be set to 0 days for logs on request), lowest ops friction.
- Dedicated: 4–6 weeks to reserve and validate capacity (region dependent). Pricing band: $XXk–$YYk/month depending on GPU class and commitment. Includes SLA 99.9% with credits per SOW_redlines.pdf.
- Private (VPC): 6–8 weeks typical; includes KMS integration (+ additional 1–2 weeks if HSM requested). One-time setup fee indicated in the MAP.

Cross-region/failover guidance: we recommend active-passive with automated routing and warm-standby in a secondary region; cost depends on standby capacity sizing. We included two fallback options in the MAP: cold failover (cheaper, longer RTO) and warm-standby (higher cost, low RTO).

I added the procurement calendar and a proposed decision window: target decision week starting 2026-08-10 (about 8 weeks) with an option to accelerate to 2026-07-20 if signatures come through this month.
